queueProposal.summary: R15 retains a D3DSBT_ALL state block across ResetEx and applies it afterward. Microsoft Direct3D 9 Reset guidance explicitly requires state blocks associated with the device to be released before Reset. Remove the persistent state-block dependency from the reset boundary; preserve/replay the baseline through explicit value snapshots or a post-Reset state object only after Reset succeeds.

SkyGlow ping-pong source selection is reversed: bright writes temp, horizontal blur writes reduced, so one-step must composite reduced; optional vertical blur writes temp, so two-step must composite temp. Current code does the opposite in both cases. SkyGlowFactor=1 therefore composites the pre-horizontal-blur temp texture.
Retain as lower priority after reset/SkyGlow: R33 screen-space classification can be threaded into HUD handling to avoid duplicate classification work.

keyEvidence.integrationHead: vr-d3d9ex-focus is 8cca78df85fef21a38e66f20fcf9ae867c4779cb, including the integrated XYZRHW final-owner dispatch fix.
reset: R15CaptureClassicExtraBaseline creates and stores R15ClassicAllState via CreateStateBlock(D3DSBT_ALL).
ResetCompatDeviceR15 calls the lower ResetEx path while R15ClassicAllState is still retained, then R15RestoreClassicAllState calls Apply on that same object.
Microsoft IDirect3DDevice9::Reset documentation says applications should release state blocks associated with the device before Reset; Reset also loses all state information.
CreateStateBlock documentation confirms D3D9 captures requested state values at object creation, so this object is a pre-reset snapshot rather than a post-reset reconstruction.
skyGlow: Bright pass: source reduced -> destination temp.
Horizontal blur: source temp -> destination reduced.
effectiveTwoStep=false initializes compositeSource=temp, skipping horizontal blur output.
effectiveTwoStep=true performs vertical blur source reduced -> destination temp but then sets compositeSource=reduced, skipping vertical blur output.
